summary: This UK Radiators buying-guide article explains low surface temperature (LST) radiators, which stay cool enough to touch to reduce scald and burn risk in settings such as schools, nurseries, offices and hospitals. It describes how LSTs decouple the emitter and pipework from the casing so no surface exceeds 43℃, contrasts this with a typical steel radiator that can reach 80℃, and outlines the two LST types the company sells: Type 11 (K1) and Type 22 (K2). The rest of the page is site navigation, promotions and footer boilerplate.
one_line: A UK Radiators guide to low surface temperature radiators, their 43℃ safety limit, and the Type 11 and Type 22 models.
key_facts: Low surface temperature radiators (LSTs) do not heat up past 43℃ on their surface and remain safe to touch to help prevent scalds and burns.
A typical steel radiator can reach up to 80℃ on its surface, while the standard radiator warning is 120℃ within compliance.
In an LST radiator the emitter and pipework are decoupled from the casing, so no part of the surface exceeds 43℃.
Because of this design, an LST continues to meet safety standards even if the thermostat fails.
The article references HSE guidance titled "Managing the risks from hot water and surfaces in health and social care".
LSTs are suited to schools, nurseries, offices and hospitals, where health and safety may be a concern.
The UK Radiators range meets NHS guidance of "safe hot water and surface temperature".
All UK Radiators LST radiators are finished with anti-bacterial paint as standard.
UK Radiators sells two types of LST radiator: Type 11 (also known as K1) and Type 22 (known as K2).
Type 11 LST radiators combine a single front heating panel with one set of convector fins, giving a slimline profile.
Type 11 radiators are described as ideal for heating a small space quickly and efficiently, and are a little kinder to the wallet.
Type 22 radiators feature twin heating panels that sandwich two sets of convector fins and are designed for high heat outputs in large spaces.
Type 22 radiators conform to BS EN 442 standards and are guaranteed to perform at pressure up to 8 bar.
The article advises using the site's BTU calculator to work out what size radiator is needed.
The Type 22 product image is labelled K2 LST - Type 22 Low Surface Temperature Convector Radiator - H800mm x W1960mm.
